question: Which of the following State governments has launched a scheme 'Ankur' in May 2021 to promote planting of trees in public, wherein people will be awarded for planting and taking care of the saplings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Madhya Pradesh government launched the 'Ankur' scheme in May 2021 to promote tree plantation, under which people are rewarded for planting and nurturing saplings. (अंकुर योजना — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The scheme was launched by the state's Forest Department to increase green cover and involve citizens directly in afforestation through a reward-based mechanism tied to caring for the sapling over time, not just planting it.

 

• Participants can register their planted saplings and monetary or other incentives are given based on the survival and growth of the trees over subsequent years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh has run several welfare and environment-linked schemes, illustrating the state's mix of initiatives in the agriculture and afforestation space.

 

• Other states run their own plantation drives, e.g. Haryana's 'Panchvati' scheme and Telangana's 'Haritha Haram', but the specific 'Ankur' reward-based scheme of May 2021 belongs to Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Known for its Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali Abhiyan, a broader water and greening mission, not the 'Ankur' scheme.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Runs afforestation efforts under its own state programmes, not 'Ankur'.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Focuses on Himalayan afforestation and eco-task forces, but did not launch the 'Ankur' scheme.

question: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, the thumb is directed towards the direction of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is current.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right-Hand Thumb Rule (also called Maxwell's rule or Ampere's rule) states that if a current-carrying conductor is held in the right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of current flow, the curled fingers indicate the direction of the magnetic field around the conductor. (दायें हाथ का अंगूठा नियम — धारा की दिशा)

 

• It is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field lines produced around a straight current-carrying wire.

 

• This rule is a mnemonic closely linked to Ampere's circuital law and is widely used in electromagnetism to relate current direction and magnetic field direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related rule, Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, is used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field (motor effect).

 

• Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is used to find the direction of induced current in a conductor moving through a magnetic field (generator effect).

 

NOTE

 

• Electric field (Option 2): The right-hand thumb rule is not used for electric field direction; it applies specifically to current and its associated magnetic field.

 

• Motion of the conductor (Option 3): This is the basis of Fleming's right-hand rule (generator rule), not the right-hand thumb rule.

 

• Magnetic field (Option 4): In the right-hand thumb rule, the magnetic field is represented by the curl of the fingers, not the thumb; the thumb represents current.

question:
Match the following Sportsman in List I and Award in List II:

List I - Sportsman

A. Devendra Jhajharia

B. Sumit Antil

C. Neeraj Chopra

D. Shikhar Dhawan

List II - Award

i. Padma Shri 2022

ii. Padma Bhushan 2022

iii. Arjun Award 2021

iv. Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021
solution_text:
The correct answer is A-ii, B-i, C-iv, D-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Devendra Jhajharia (Paralympic javelin thrower) was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2022. (देवेंद्र झाझरिया — पद्म भूषण 2022)

 

• Sumit Antil (Paralympic javelin gold medallist, Tokyo 2020) received the Padma Shri in 2022.

 

• Neeraj Chopra (Olympic gold medallist, javelin, Tokyo 2020) received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021, India's highest sporting honour.

 

• Shikhar Dhawan (cricketer) received the Arjuna Award in 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honour, renamed from the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award in 2021.

 

• The Arjuna Award recognises consistently outstanding performance in a sport over a four-year period, while the Padma awards (Shri/Bhushan/Vibhushan) are the country's civilian honours.

 

NOTE

 

• The other combinations (Options 2, 3 and 4) mismatch these sportspersons with the wrong award/year for this specific set of honours, e.g. pairing Jhajharia with the Arjuna Award 2021 or Chopra with the Padma Shri 2022, which is factually incorrect.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution CANNOT be suspended even during an emergency declared on the grounds of war or external aggression?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 20 and 21.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 359 of the Indian Constitution allows the President to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency, except Articles 20 and 21. (अनुच्छेद 20 और 21 — आपातकाल में निलंबित नहीं)

 

• Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences (no ex-post-facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination), and Article 21 guarantees the right to life and personal liberty.

 

• This safeguard was strengthened by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, enacted after the experience of the 1975 Emergency, to ensure these two rights remain enforceable even during an emergency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Emergency provisions are covered under Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) of the Constitution, dealing with National Emergency (Art. 352), President's Rule (Art. 356) and Financial Emergency (Art. 360).

 

• The landmark Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978) case expanded the scope of Article 21 to include the right to live with dignity, not merely animal existence.

 

NOTE

 

• Articles 15 and 17 (Option 1): Deal with prohibition of discrimination and abolition of untouchability respectively; both can be suspended during an emergency.

 

• Articles 14 and 16 (Option 3): Guarantee equality before law and equality of opportunity in public employment; both are suspendable during an emergency.

 

• Articles 30 and 32 (Option 4): Article 30 relates to minority rights to establish educational institutions and Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies; both can be suspended, unlike Articles 20 and 21.

question: Which of the following is the largest inhabited riverine island in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Majuli.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Majuli, located in the Brahmaputra River in Assam, is the largest inhabited riverine (river) island in the world. (माजुली — विश्व का सबसे बड़ा नदी द्वीप)

 

• It was granted the status of a separate district of Assam in 2016 and is known for its Neo-Vaishnavite Satras (monasteries) established by Srimanta Sankardeva.

 

• Majuli's area has been shrinking over the years due to erosion by the Brahmaputra, and it was formed at the confluence of the Brahmaputra, Subansiri and other rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Majuli is famous for mask-making, pottery (by the Deori and Mishing communities), and the traditional Sattriya dance, which originated in its monasteries.

 

• Assam's Brahmaputra is known for forming numerous river islands and sandbars along its course.

 

NOTE

 

• Peacock (Option 1): A small island in the Brahmaputra near Guwahati housing the Umananda Temple; it is not the largest riverine island.

 

• Bhavani (Option 3): Not recognised as the world's largest riverine island; this is a distractor option.

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 4): A group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea, not a riverine island.

question: In which year was the battle of Buxar fought?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1764.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764 between the forces of the British East India Company (led by Hector Munro) and the combined army of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), and Shah Alam II (Mughal Emperor). (बक्सर का युद्ध — 1764)

 

• The British victory at Buxar was decisive and led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), under which the Company obtained the Diwani (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

• This battle is often considered more significant than the Battle of Plassey (1757) in establishing British political and economic dominance in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) was signed separately with Shah Alam II and Shuja-ud-Daulah by Robert Clive.

 

• The defeat at Buxar marked the effective end of any serious combined Indian resistance to British expansion in eastern India for decades.

 

NOTE

 

• 1793 (Option 1): The year of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal under Lord Cornwallis, unrelated to the Battle of Buxar.

 

• 1777 (Option 2): Not associated with any major Anglo-Indian battle of this significance.

 

• 1757 (Option 4): The year of the Battle of Plassey, not Buxar.

question: What was the main objective of the Second Green Revolution in India?
option_1: Ensuring food security in the western states
option_3: Focusing on holistic development in agriculture
option_4: Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides
solution_text:
The correct answer is Focusing on holistic development in agriculture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second Green Revolution in India aims at a more holistic, sustainable, and inclusive approach to agricultural development, moving beyond the narrow yield-focused strategy of the first Green Revolution. (दूसरी हरित क्रांति — समग्र कृषि विकास)

 

• It emphasises crop diversification, sustainable use of natural resources, soil health, water conservation, and balanced regional development, rather than concentrating only on wheat and rice in a few states.

 

• The approach also seeks to extend the benefits of agricultural growth to eastern and other lagging states, and to small and marginal farmers who were largely bypassed by the first Green Revolution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Green Revolution (1960s-70s), led by M.S. Swaminathan, focused on high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation, mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

 

• Programmes like Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) reflect the goals of the Second Green Revolution.

 

NOTE

 

• Ensuring food security in the western states (Option 1): The first Green Revolution already concentrated on western/northern states; the second aims to correct this imbalance, not reinforce it.

 

• Promoting conventional agricultural practices (Option 2): The Second Green Revolution promotes newer, more sustainable practices, not conventional ones.

 

• Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides (Option 4): This describes the first Green Revolution's approach, which the second revolution seeks to move away from due to soil degradation concerns.

question: Who among the following was the youngest recipient of the Sangeetha Kalanidhi awarded by the Music Academy in 1947?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Semmangudi Radhakrishna Srinivasa Iyer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Semmangudi Radhakrishna Srinivasa Iyer, the renowned Carnatic vocalist, was conferred the Sangeetha Kalanidhi by the Music Academy, Chennai (Madras) in 1947 at the age of about 39, making him its youngest recipient. (संगीत कलानिधि — सेम्मंगुडी श्रीनिवास अय्यर)

 

• The Sangeetha Kalanidhi is the highest honour conferred annually by the Music Academy, Madras, since 1929, recognising outstanding contribution to Carnatic music.

 

• Semmangudi Iyer went on to become one of the most influential figures of 20th century Carnatic music and headed the Swati Tirunal Academy of Music, Thiruvananthapuram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Semmangudi Iyer was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1968) and Padma Vibhushan (1998) for his contribution to music.

 

• Other legendary Carnatic vocalists honoured with the Sangeetha Kalanidhi include Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar and M.S. Subbulakshmi (the first woman recipient, in 1968).

 

NOTE

 

• Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar (Option 2): A pioneering Carnatic vocalist and Sangeetha Kalanidhi awardee (1938), but not the youngest recipient of the 1947 award.

 

• Mallikarjun Bheemarayappa Mansur (Option 3): A celebrated Hindustani classical vocalist of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana, unrelated to the Music Academy's Sangeetha Kalanidhi.

 

• Bhimsen Joshi (Option 4): A legendary Hindustani classical vocalist (Bharat Ratna, 2008), not associated with the Carnatic Sangeetha Kalanidhi award.

question: In Newlands' Octaves, the properties of lithium and ________ were found to be the same.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sodium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• John Newlands' Law of Octaves (1866) stated that when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic mass, every eighth element has properties similar to the first, like the notes of a musical octave. (न्यूलैंड्स के अष्टक नियम — लीथियम और सोडियम)

 

• In Newlands' arrangement, lithium (Li) was the first element, and the eighth element, sodium (Na), was found to have similar chemical properties to lithium — both being alkali metals.

 

• Similarly, beryllium and magnesium formed another such pair in his table, though the law broke down for heavier elements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newlands' Law of Octaves worked reasonably well only up to calcium; beyond that, the periodicity broke down, which was one of its major limitations.

 

• The law was an important precursor to Mendeleev's Periodic Table (1869), which arranged elements by atomic mass into a more comprehensive periodic system.

 

NOTE

 

• Aluminium (Option 2): Belongs to a different group (boron group) and was not paired with lithium in Newlands' octaves.

 

• Magnesium (Option 3): Paired with beryllium in Newlands' law, not lithium.

 

• Beryllium (Option 4): Paired with magnesium, not lithium, in Newlands' octaves.

question: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MV = PT.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Irving Fisher's Equation of Exchange is given as MV = PT, where M is the money supply, V is the velocity of circulation of money, P is the general price level, and T is the total volume of transactions. (फिशर का विनिमय समीकरण — MV = PT)

 

• This equation forms the basis of the Quantity Theory of Money, which states that the general price level is directly proportional to the quantity of money in circulation, assuming V and T remain constant.

 

• Fisher presented this theory in his 1911 book 'The Purchasing Power of Money'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A modern variant of the equation replaces total transactions (T) with real output (Y), giving MV = PY, used in macroeconomic analysis of inflation.

 

• The Cambridge cash-balance approach (Marshall, Pigou) is an alternative formulation of the quantity theory of money, expressed as M = kPY.

 

NOTE

 

• MT = VP (Option 2): This is an incorrect rearrangement of the variables and does not represent Fisher's equation.

 

• M = S + I (Option 3): This resembles the savings-investment identity in national income accounting, unrelated to Fisher's equation of exchange.

 

• M/V = T/P (Option 4): This is not a valid rearrangement of Fisher's equation; correctly rearranging MV = PT gives M/T = P/V, not M/V = T/P.

question: Which web portal was launched by the Department of Telecommunications for sharing information on mobile towers and EMF emission compliance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tarang Sanchar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tarang Sanchar is a web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, to share information on the location of mobile towers and their compliance with Electromagnetic Field (EMF) emission norms. (तरंग संचार पोर्टल — मोबाइल टावर EMF जानकारी)

 

• The portal allows citizens to check whether mobile towers in their locality comply with prescribed EMF radiation limits and to raise self-certification-based complaints.

 

• It was launched to increase transparency and address public concerns regarding the safety of mobile tower radiation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's EMF radiation exposure limits are set 10 times stricter than the international norms recommended by the ICNIRP (International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection).

 

• DoT also runs the Sanchar Saathi portal for citizen-centric telecom services like tracing lost/stolen mobile phones and checking mobile connections issued in one's name.

 

NOTE

 

• E-Amrit (Option 1): A portal on electric vehicles run by NITI Aayog, unrelated to mobile towers.

 

• Namaste (Option 2): Refers to the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme, unrelated to telecom towers.

 

• PM-Daksh (Option 4): A skill development scheme for marginalised groups under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, unrelated to telecom.

question: Which of the following Acts passed under Warren Hastings was also called 'half-loaf system'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pitt's India Act 1784.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pitt's India Act, 1784, passed during Warren Hastings' tenure as Governor-General, is popularly called the 'half-loaf' system, since it created a system of dual/double government — neither the British Crown nor the East India Company had complete control over Indian administration. (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट 1784 — 'हाफ-लोफ' व्यवस्था)

 

• It established a Board of Control in London to oversee the Company's political, civil and military affairs, while the Court of Directors continued to manage commercial affairs — hence a divided or 'half' control.

 

• This Act is regarded as the first step towards parliamentary control over the East India Company's administration in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pitt's India Act, 1784 was passed by British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.

 

• The dual system created by this Act continued (with modifications) until the Government of India Act, 1858, which finally transferred power to the British Crown after the 1857 revolt.

 

NOTE

 

• Government of India Act 1858 (Option 2): Ended East India Company rule entirely and transferred power directly to the British Crown; it was not passed under Warren Hastings and is not called the 'half-loaf' system.

 

• Charter Act 1813 (Option 3): Ended the Company's trade monopoly in India (except tea and China trade) and allowed Christian missionaries into India; unrelated to the 'half-loaf' description.

 

• Regulating Act 1773 (Option 4): The first Act of the British Parliament to regulate the Company's affairs, creating the post of Governor-General of Bengal, but it is not the Act referred to as the 'half-loaf' system.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that 'The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 43.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 43 of the Indian Constitution, under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), states that the State shall endeavour to secure a living wage and to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas. (अनुच्छेद 43 — ग्रामीण कुटीर उद्योग)

 

• This provision reflects the Gandhian philosophy of village self-sufficiency (swaraj) and decentralised, rural-based economic development.

 

• Directive Principles like Article 43 are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country as per Article 37.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 43-A (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976) provides for workers' participation in management of industries.

 

• Article 43-B (added by the 97th Amendment, 2011) promotes co-operative societies.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 44 (Option 1): Relates to the State's endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens across India.

 

• Article 49 (Option 2): Relates to the protection of monuments and places of national importance.

 

• Article 42 (Option 4): Relates to provisions for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

question: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President's rule in any state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 356.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 356 of the Indian Constitution provides for the imposition of President's Rule in a state if the President is satisfied that the state government cannot function in accordance with constitutional provisions. (अनुच्छेद 356 — राष्ट्रपति शासन)

 

• It is widely regarded as the most controversial/misused Article because it has often been invoked for political reasons rather than genuine constitutional breakdown, a concern highlighted by the Sarkaria Commission and the landmark S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994) case.

 

• The Bommai judgment made the imposition of President's Rule subject to judicial review and required floor tests to prove majority, curbing its arbitrary use.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under Article 356, President's Rule initially lasts 6 months and can be extended up to a maximum of 3 years, subject to parliamentary approval every 6 months (with additional conditions after one year, per the 44th Amendment).

 

• During President's Rule, the state's executive authority is exercised by the Governor on behalf of the President, and the State Legislative Assembly is either dissolved or kept in suspended animation.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 358 (Option 1): Deals with the suspension of Fundamental Rights under Article 19 during a National Emergency.

 

• Article 360 (Option 3): Provides for the declaration of a Financial Emergency.

 

• Article 352 (Option 4): Provides for the declaration of a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

question: In 1539, the Battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Shah Suri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Chausa (1539) was fought between the Mughal emperor Humayun and Sher Shah Suri (then known as Sher Khan) on the banks of the Ganges near Chausa, Bihar. (चौसा का युद्ध — हुमायूं और शेरशाह सूरी)

 

• Sher Shah Suri won the battle, forcing Humayun to flee, and this victory paved the way for the establishment of the Sur Empire.

 

• Humayun was decisively defeated again by Sher Shah at the Battle of Kannauj/Bilgram (1540), after which he was forced into exile for about 15 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur dynasty and is remembered for major administrative reforms — the Rupiya (silver coin), the Grand Trunk Road, and a well-organised revenue and postal system.

 

• Humayun eventually regained the Mughal throne in 1555 with Safavid Persian assistance, defeating the Suri successors.

 

NOTE

 

• Ibrahim Lodhi (Option 1): The last Lodhi Sultan, defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), not connected to the Battle of Chausa.

 

• Sikandar Suri (Option 3): A later Suri ruler defeated by Akbar at the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).

 

• Rana Sanga (Option 4): The Rajput ruler defeated by Babur at the Battle of Khanwa (1527).

question: India hosted the Asian Games in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951 and 1982.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India has hosted the Asian Games twice, both times in New Delhi — the very first Asian Games in 1951 and the 9th Asian Games in 1982. (एशियाई खेल — 1951 और 1982, नई दिल्ली)

 

• The 1951 Asian Games were the inaugural edition of the event, held at the National Stadium, New Delhi.

 

• The 1982 Asian Games were notable for the construction of major sporting infrastructure, including the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, and were the first Asian Games telecast live in colour television in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Asian Games are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and held every four years.

 

• India has not hosted the Asian Games again since 1982.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 all include the incorrect year 1954 or 1986, neither of which India hosted the Asian Games in; the correct pair is only 1951 and 1982.

question: A dense mass of water drops on smoke or dust particles in the lower atmosphere layers is referred to as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is smog.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Smog is a dense mass of water droplets condensed on smoke or dust particles suspended in the lower layers of the atmosphere, formed by a mixture of smoke and fog. (स्मॉग — धुआं और कोहरे का मिश्रण)

 

• Smog is typically associated with air pollution, particularly in urban and industrial areas, and can be classified as photochemical smog (from vehicle/industrial emissions reacting with sunlight) or sulphurous smog (from burning coal).

 

• It significantly reduces visibility and poses serious respiratory health hazards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Delhi's winter smog is a recurring environmental issue, driven by vehicular emissions, stubble burning in neighbouring states, and low wind speeds trapping pollutants.

 

• The term 'smog' was coined in the early 20th century by combining the words 'smoke' and 'fog'.

 

NOTE

 

• Mist (Option 1): A thin, light fog formed by condensation of water vapour, not specifically associated with smoke/dust particles.

 

• Blizzard (Option 2): A severe snowstorm with high winds and low visibility, unrelated to smoke/dust.

 

• Frost (Option 3): A deposit of ice crystals formed when water vapour condenses and freezes on a cold surface, not water drops on smoke/dust particles.

question: Sardhana Christian Fair is held in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sardhana Christian Fair is held annually at Sardhana, in Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh. (सरधना ईसाई मेला — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• It is centred around the Basilica of Our Lady of Graces, built by Begum Samru, a historic figure associated with the town of Sardhana.

 

• The fair attracts pilgrims and devotees from across the region and is one of the notable Christian religious fairs of North India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Begum Samru (Farzana Zeb-un-Nissa) was a prominent 18th-19th century figure who ruled the principality of Sardhana and later converted to Christianity, commissioning the basilica.

 

• Uttar Pradesh hosts many other major religious fairs, including the Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj and the Magh Mela.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1), Haryana (Option 2) and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): None of these states host the Sardhana Christian Fair; the fair and its associated basilica are specifically located at Sardhana in Uttar Pradesh.

question: Ali Akbar Khan was associated with which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maihar gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, a legendary sarod maestro, belonged to the Maihar gharana, founded by his father and guru, Ustad Allauddin Khan. (मैहर घराना — उस्ताद अली अकबर खान)

 

• The Maihar gharana is renowned for its emphasis on instrumental music and produced several stalwarts, including Pandit Ravi Shankar (sitar) and Pandit Nikhil Banerjee, all trained under Allauddin Khan.

 

• Ali Akbar Khan received the Padma Vibhushan (1989) and multiple Grammy nominations for his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ali Akbar Khan founded the Ali Akbar College of Music in Kolkata (1956) and later in California, USA, to popularise Indian classical music globally.

 

• Violinist Yehudi Menuhin recognised him as one of the greatest musicians in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Agra gharana (Option 2): A vocal gharana known for its nom-tom alap and dhrupad-ang khayal style, associated with vocalists like Ustad Faiyaz Khan.

 

• Gwalior gharana (Option 3): The oldest khayal gharana, associated with vocalists such as Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

 

• Kirana gharana (Option 4): A vocal gharana known for sur (note purity) and slow, meditative alap, associated with Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Pandit Bhimsen Joshi.

question: Which of the following movements created regional disparities between large and small farmers in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Green revolution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution (1960s-70s) in India, though it dramatically boosted foodgrain production, is widely criticised for creating regional disparities — concentrating benefits in irrigated states like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern and rain-fed regions lagged behind. (हरित क्रांति — क्षेत्रीय असमानता)

 

• It also widened the gap between large farmers (who could afford HYV seeds, fertilizers, irrigation and machinery) and small/marginal farmers, who often lacked access to these inputs and credit.

 

• This unequal impact was one of the key motivations behind the later 'Second Green Revolution' push for more inclusive, region-balanced agricultural growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India is credited to agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

 

• Programmes like RKVY (Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana) and BGREI were later launched to correct the regional imbalances left by the Green Revolution.

 

NOTE

 

• Yellow revolution (Option 2): Relates to growth in oilseed/edible oil production, not linked with the large-small farmer disparity debate to the same extent.

 

• Pink revolution (Option 3): Relates to growth in meat and poultry (including buffalo meat) processing/exports.

 

• Blue revolution (Option 4): Relates to growth in fish and aquaculture production.

question: Elelakkaradi dance of Kerala is performed by which of the following tribes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Irular tribe.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Elelakkaradi dance is a traditional tribal dance form of Kerala, performed by the Irular tribe. (एलेलक्करडी नृत्य — इरुलर जनजाति)

 

• The Irular tribe is one of the indigenous tribal communities found in the hilly and forested regions of Kerala (also present in Tamil Nadu), traditionally associated with agriculture, hunting-gathering and forest-based livelihoods.

 

• Elelakkaradi and other tribal dances are performed during festivals and ceremonial occasions, reflecting the community's cultural heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala's other notable tribal dances include Kolattam, Kotiyattam and Kummi, performed by various tribal and folk communities across the state.

 

• Kerala is home to several tribal groups such as the Kurumba, Kadar, Muthuvan and Paniya, each with distinct cultural traditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Kurumba tribe (Option 2): A tribal community found in the Nilgiri hill region, known for their own distinct dance and honey-gathering traditions, not associated with Elelakkaradi.

 

• Adiyan tribe (Option 3): A tribal community of Wayanad, traditionally associated with agricultural labour, not linked to the Elelakkaradi dance.

 

• Mavilan tribe (Option 4): A tribal community of northern Kerala known for Theyyam-related ritual performances, not for the Elelakkaradi dance.

question: Which of the following illustrations is related to chloroplasts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Illustration 'c' shows an oval, double-membrane-bound structure containing internal stacks of disc-shaped structures — this represents a chloroplast, with the stacks corresponding to grana (thylakoid stacks) embedded in the stroma. (क्लोरोप्लास्ट — हरितलवक)

 

• Chloroplasts are the site of photosynthesis in plant cells, containing the green pigment chlorophyll within the thylakoid membranes.

 

• Each granum is a stack of flattened, disc-like thylakoids, and adjacent grana are connected by tubular structures called stroma lamellae.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chloroplasts, like mitochondria, are semi-autonomous organelles possessing their own circular DNA and ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic theory of their origin.

 

• The oval shape and double membrane in illustration 'c' closely resembles standard textbook diagrams of a chloroplast cross-section.

 

NOTE

 

• Illustration 'a' (Option 1): Depicts a star-shaped cell with a nucleus-like central body, resembling a connective tissue cell, not a chloroplast.

 

• Illustration 'd' (Option 3): Depicts a multicellular tissue diagram with labelled nucleus and cells, representing plant tissue, not a single chloroplast.

 

• Illustration 'b' (Option 4): Depicts a cross-shaped patterned structure resembling a stylised abstract shape, not a chloroplast.

question: Who among the following generally used to head the provincial administration under the Mauryas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Mauryan administration, provinces (called Janapadas) were generally headed by a royal prince known as the Kumara (or Aryaputra), who acted as a viceroy on behalf of the emperor. (कुमार — मौर्य प्रांतीय प्रशासन)

 

• The Ashokan edicts mention Kumaras governing key provincial capitals such as Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri.

 

• The Kumara was assisted by a council of ministers (Mahamatyas) and other officials in provincial administration, mirroring the structure of the central government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mauryan Empire (322-185 BCE) was divided into major provinces headed by Kumaras and smaller administrative units headed by officials like Rajukas and Pradeshikas.

 

• Chief sources for Mauryan administration include Kautilya's Arthashastra, Megasthenes' Indica, and the Ashokan edicts.

 

NOTE

 

• Dandapala (Option 1): An official associated with police/law and order administration at the local level, not the head of a province.

 

• Samaharta (Option 3): The chief revenue collection officer at the central level under the Mauryas, akin to a finance minister.

 

• Prashasti (Option 4): Not a Mauryan administrative post; the term generally refers to eulogistic royal inscriptions/praise-poems in ancient Indian epigraphy.

question: Which is the most important protein component in milk, both quantitatively and nutritionally, that accounts for about 80% of the total protein in bovine milk?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Casein.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Casein is the most important protein in milk, both quantitatively and nutritionally, accounting for about 80% of the total protein content in bovine (cow) milk. (कैसीन — दूध का प्रमुख प्रोटीन)

 

• Casein exists in milk as micelles (colloidal particles) and is responsible for the characteristic white colour of milk; it is precipitated by acid or the enzyme rennin, forming the basis of cheese and paneer production.

 

• The remaining milk proteins are collectively called whey proteins (including lactalbumin and lactoglobulin), making up about 20% of total milk protein.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Casein is rich in essential amino acids and phosphorus, making it a complete, high-quality protein important in infant and human nutrition.

 

• Milk also contains other components such as lactose (milk sugar), fats, vitamins (A, D, B12) and minerals like calcium.

 

NOTE

 

• Actin (Option 1): A structural protein found in muscle cells (part of the actin-myosin contractile system), not a milk protein.

 

• Albumin (Option 2): A minor whey protein present in milk (lactalbumin) but not the major/most important one; blood/egg albumin is a different, distinct protein.

 

• Pepsin (Option 3): A digestive enzyme secreted in the stomach that breaks down proteins, not a milk protein itself.
